summary: Ben Joffe works in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Colorado under the supervision of Carole McGranahan.

Benedetta Lomi works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London (~2007–2012) and taught at the University of Virginia (~2014–2018) before taking a post at the University of Bristol in ~2018.

Benimadhab Barua (1888–1948) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Presidency University, Calcutta, and the University of London (D.Litt., ~1914–1917), he was headmaster at Mahamuni Anglo-Pali Institution (1912) and a professor at the University of Calcutta (1918–1948).

Benjamin A. Elman (b. 1946) is a Sinologist and historian who earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Nathan Sivin and Susan Naquin. He taught at UCLA (1986–2002) and became Director of Princeton's East Asian Studies Program in 2002.
Benjamin Bogin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr., having also studied under Janet Gyatso and Gareth Sparham.

Benjamin Brose specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Stanford (~2003–2009) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, and became an assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan in ~2009.
Benjamin W. Fortson IV specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Yale University and Harvard University (~1992–1996) and held a post at the University of Michigan in ~2003.
Benjamin Wood specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Toronto under doctoral supervisor Frances Garrett.

Benkyo Shiio (1876–1971) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He served as president of Taisho University (1926), head of Sanko Research Institute (~1948–1971), and head of Sanko Library (~1963–1968).

Benoytosh Bhattacharyya (1897–1964) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. After earning degrees from the University of Calcutta (MA, 1919) and University of Dhaka (PhD, 1925), he served as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, starting in 1927.

Benoît Vermander (b. 1960) specializes in Sinology and religious studies. Educated at Yale, Sciences Po, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Centre Sèvres, he served as Academic Director of the Taipei Ricci Institute (1996–2009) and professor at Fudan University (2009).

Bernard Faure (b. 1948) works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his Doctorat d’État at the University of Paris/Paris Diderot, and held professorial posts at Cornell (~1983–1987), Stanford (~1987–2006), and Columbia University (~2006–2021).

Bernard Frank (1927–1996) was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Rolf A. Stein. He served as head of Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1972–1974) and held the Japanese Civilization chair at Collège de France (1979–1996).

Bernard Williams (1929–2003) was a philosopher who studied at Balliol College, Oxford (~1947–1951). He held academic posts at University College London (~1964–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1988–2003).
Bernd Schneidmüller (b. 1954) is a historian and archaeologist. He held posts at the University of Oldenburg (~1987–1992) and Heidelberg University (~2003).

Bernfried Schlerath (1924–2003) worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics, studying under Paul Thieme (~1950–1954). He held posts at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1956–1964), University of Marburg (~1964–1969), and Free University of Berlin (~1969–1992).
Bernhard Breloer (1894–1947) was an Indology scholar. He succeeded Heinrich Lüders and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1933–1945).

Bernhard Forssman (b. 1934) is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Karl Hoffmann at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1955–1964) and held posts at the University of Marburg (1968–1983) and Erlangen-Nürnberg (1983).

Bernhard Geiger (1881–1964) specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. After studying at Vienna, Bonn, Göttingen, and Heidelberg, he taught at the University of Vienna (~1909–1938), Asia Institute (1938–1951), and Columbia University (1951–1953).

Bernhard Hirzel (1807–1847) was an Indologist who studied under Franz Bopp in Berlin and graduated from Göttingen. He studied at Zurich and Paris, and held lecturer posts at the University of Zurich in 1833, 1835–1837, and 1845.
